g.title:
Create a high-level Azure cloud architecture diagram for an AI-powered Infrastructure Modernization Platform with MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration: Core Components:
Primary Input Layer:
Legacy Infrastructure Repositories (600+ repos: 400 Terraform, 200 BICEP) GitHub/Azure DevOps repositories Source code and infrastructure-as-code files
AI Reference Knowledge Base (via MCP):
Confluence MCP Server (organizational standards, internal documentation) PDF MCP Server (best practices guides, migration playbooks) ServiceNow MCP Server (approved patterns, change management policies, CMDB) Microsoft Well-Architected Framework MCP Server (Azure design principles) Azure Verified Modules Documentation MCP Server (AVM standards and templates) MCP Context Aggregation Service
AI Processing Engine:
Azure OpenAI Service (GPT-4) - code analysis and transformation MCP Context Injection - enriches prompts with guidance from knowledge base Azure Cognitive Services - document understanding and pattern recognition Migration logic and transformation rules engine
Application/Orchestration Layer:
Azure Container Apps - migration orchestration service API Management - service exposure and gateway Workflow Engine - migration pipeline coordination Validation and Quality Gates service
Data/State Layer:
Azure SQL Database - migration tracking, audit logs, metadata Azure Storage Account (Blob) - staged repositories, transformation artifacts Azure Cosmos DB - MCP context cache and session management Azure Redis Cache - performance optimization
Output Layer:
Azure Verified Modules (AVM) compliant code Transformed infrastructure code Migration reports and documentation Compliance validation results
Supporting Infrastructure:
Azure Monitor & Application Insights - observability and diagnostics Azure Key Vault - secrets and credentials management Azure Virtual Network - network isolation Azure Private Endpoints - secure connectivity Azure DevOps/GitHub Actions - CI/CD automation
Architecture Requirements:
Clearly distinguish PRIMARY INPUT (Terraform/BICEP repos) from REFERENCE SOURCES (Confluence, PDF, SNOW, WAF, AVM docs) Show how MCP servers provide contextual guidance to Azure OpenAI during transformation Display the flow: Legacy Code → AI Analysis (with MCP guidance) → AVM Output Indicate how reference sources improve transformation quality and compliance Show real-time MCP context retrieval during migration processing Highlight the feedback loop where AI queries reference sources for decision-making
Visual Style:
Use official Azure icon set Differentiate visually between:
PRIMARY DATA FLOW (bold/solid lines): Terraform/BICEP → Processing → AVM REFERENCE/GUIDANCE FLOW (dashed lines): Knowledge sources → MCP → AI enrichment
Color-code layers: Input (blue), MCP/Reference (green), AI Processing (purple), Storage (orange), Output (red) Use clear directional arrows with labels Show MCP as middleware providing "just-in-time" context
Key Technical Details:
Mark MCP servers as "read-only reference" vs "processing pipeline" Show how AI queries MCP knowledge base during each transformation Indicate context enrichment: "AI asks: 'What's the AVM pattern for this?' → MCP retrieves → AI applies" Display async patterns for reference data caching Show phased rollout (Year 1: Terraform 400 repos, Year 2: BICEP 200 repos, Year 3: Custom AVM)
Layout Guidance:
Top section: Reference Knowledge Sources (Confluence, PDF, SNOW, WAF, AVM docs) connected via MCP Center section: Main processing flow (Legacy Repos → AI + MCP → Transformed Code) Bottom section: Azure infrastructure services (storage, monitoring, security) Clearly show MCP as the "brain/memory" that AI consults during transformation
g.text: Create a high-level Azure cloud architecture diagram for an AI-powered Infrastructure Modernization Platform with MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration:
Legacy Infrastructure Repositories (600+ repos: 400 Terraform, 200 BICEP)
Confluence MCP Server (organizational standards, internal documentation)
PDF MCP Server (best practices guides, migration playbooks)
ServiceNow MCP Server (approved patterns, change management policies, CMDB)
Microsoft Well-Architected Framework MCP Server (Azure design principles)
Azure Verified Modules Documentation MCP Server (AVM standards and templates)
Azure OpenAI Service (GPT-4) - code analysis and transformation
MCP Context Injection - enriches prompts with guidance from knowledge base
Azure Cognitive Services - document understanding and pattern recognition
Migration logic and transformation rules engine
Azure Container Apps - migration orchestration service
API Management - service exposure and gateway
Azure SQL Database - migration tracking, audit logs, metadata
Azure Storage Account (Blob) - staged repositories, transformation artifacts
Azure Cosmos DB - MCP context cache and session management
Azure Monitor & Application Insights - observability and diagnostics
Azure Key Vault - secrets and credentials management
Clearly distinguish PRIMARY INPUT (Terraform/BICEP repos) from REFERENCE SOURCES (Confluence, PDF, SNOW, WAF, AVM docs)
Show how MCP servers provide contextual guidance to Azure OpenAI during transformation
Display the flow: Legacy Code → AI Analysis (with MCP guidance) → AVM Output
Indicate how reference sources improve transformation quality and compliance
Show real-time MCP context retrieval during migration processing
Highlight the feedback loop where AI queries reference sources for decision-making
PRIMARY DATA FLOW (bold/solid lines): Terraform/BICEP → Processing → AVM
REFERENCE/GUIDANCE FLOW (dashed lines): Knowledge sources → MCP → AI enrichment
Color-code layers: Input (blue), MCP/Reference (green), AI Processing (purple), Storage (orange), Output (red)
Use clear directional arrows with labels
Show MCP as middleware providing "just-in-time" context
Mark MCP servers as "read-only reference" vs "processing pipeline"
Show how AI queries MCP knowledge base during each transformation
Indicate context enrichment: "AI asks: 'What's the AVM pattern for this?' → MCP retrieves → AI applies"
Display async patterns for reference data caching
Show phased rollout (Year 1: Terraform 400 repos, Year 2: BICEP 200 repos, Year 3: Custom AVM)
Top section: Reference Knowledge Sources (Confluence, PDF, SNOW, WAF, AVM docs) connected via MCP
Center section: Main processing flow (Legacy Repos → AI + MCP → Transformed Code)
Bottom section: Azure infrastructure services (storage, monitoring, security)
Clearly show MCP as the "brain/memory" that AI consults during transformation
